WV-2026-HB5527.title: Relating to Wellness Reimbursement Programs

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 662)
Became law without Governor's signature - Senate Journal
Became law without Governor's signature- House Journal
Reported do pass, but first to Finance

WV-2026-HB5527.aiSummary: The law sets rules for wellness reimbursement programs, which are extra health or wellness benefits tied to insurance or self-insured health plans. It requires program administrators to get a state license, pay fees, keep records, and follow federal and state rules. It also gives the Insurance Commissioner power to inspect records, fine or revoke licenses, and enforce the law, and it sets penalties for violations.

WV-2026-HB5437.aiSummary: The law sets up a new license for vape or smoke shops in West Virginia and requires them to follow state rules to operate. It sets application and background check rules for owners and managers, and it limits who can get or keep a license based on certain criminal history and other qualifications. Running a shop without the license can lead to a misdemeanor charge, with a fine of up to $10,000 and jail time of up to one year.

WV-2026-HB5110.title: Amend section providing for waiver of tuition and fees for senior citizens auditing certain college classes

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 381)

WV-2026-HB5110.aiSummary: The law changes West Virginia rules for tuition and fee waivers or adjustments at public colleges for older adults who audit classes, which means take the class without credit. It lowers the age limit from 65 to 60 and says that, for the no-credit option, any extra tuition for eligible nonresident students cannot be more than 50% of the rate for West Virginia residents.

WV-2026-HB4951.title: Requiring MDs and DOs to complete continuing education

actions.text: House refused to concur; requested Senate to recede (Voice)
Committee amendments withdrawn by unanimous consent
Originating in House Health and Human Resources

WV-2026-HB4951.aiSummary: Requires doctors with MD and DO licenses to complete continuing medical education to renew their licenses. It also adds nutrition training rules for people licensed on or before July 1, 2026, and for new license holders after that date, with timing based on the next renewal or within one year of initial licensure. The measure became law in 2026.

WV-2026-HB4483.aiSummary: The law changes rules for funeral service licenses, apprentices, and funeral establishments in West Virginia. It sets or updates license and renewal rules, training and apprenticeship limits, and board powers over inspections, fees, fines, complaints, and continuing education. It also lets a funeral establishment use a provisional licensee in charge for up to 90 days in some cases and creates emeritus licenses for some older license holders.

WV-2026-HB4366.policyArea: Crime, Domestic Relations, Military and Veterans
WV-2026-HB4366.aiSummary: This law changes rules for military interpersonal violence cases. It defines some terms, lets a military protective order be used when asking for an emergency protective order or a temporary personal safety order, and requires police to notify the right agencies about possible violations of military protective orders. It applies to people involved in these military and domestic violence cases.
